rule.body: Spelling is a poor guide to vowel sounds, so listen to the sound, not the letters: seat and field share /iː/, but sit has short /ɪ/. Pairs to watch: /iː/ and /ɪ/ (seat, sit); /æ/, /ɑː/ and /ʌ/ (cat, cart, cut); /ɒ/ and /ɔː/ (cot, caught); /ʊ/ and /uː/ (full, fool); /ɜː/ (bird); and the weak /ə/ (about). Diphthongs glide from one sound to another: /eɪ/ day, /aɪ/ buy, /əʊ/ go, /aʊ/ now, /ɪə/ here, /eə/ hair.
rule.example: bird, word and heard all have /ɜː/, although they are spelt with i, o and ea.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one in [[seat]].
questions.explanation: seat and field have long /iː/; ship and fit have short /ɪ/, and bed has /e/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one in [[cat]].
questions.explanation: cat and lamp have /æ/; calm has /ɑː/, cup has /ʌ/ and cot has /ɒ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that contains the sound /ɔː/.
questions.explanation: caught has /ɔː/; hot and shop have short /ɒ/, and cup has /ʌ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one in [[bird]].
questions.explanation: bird and word have /ɜː/; card has /ɑː/, bead has /iː/ and bored has /ɔː/.

questions.stem: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others?
questions.explanation: pull has /ʊ/; cut, blood and son all have /ʌ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one in [[pool]].
questions.explanation: pool and rule have long /uː/; full, book and wood have short /ʊ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that contains the sound /əʊ/.
questions.explanation: soul has /əʊ/; now has /aʊ/, buy has /aɪ/ and saw has /ɔː/.

questions.stem: Which of these words has a different vowel sound from the others?
questions.explanation: said has /e/; great, weigh and rain all have the diphthong /eɪ/.

questions.stem: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one in [[hair]].
questions.explanation: hair and bear have /eə/; here has /ɪə/, her has /ɜː/ and hay has /eɪ/.

questions.stem: Which word has the weak vowel /ə/ in its first syllable?
questions.explanation: about begins with weak /ə/; apple begins with /æ/, under with /ʌ/ and open with /əʊ/.
